title: Two beats in Chicago versus four beats from New Orleans
summary: Chicago played two beats; the New Orleans men brought four, and Turetsky says Pops always played four, not Walter Page first.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Yeah. I wonder what happened in Chicago before the New Orleans musicians came. What went on?
Well, they played that, you know, Chicago style. Two beats, you know.
We come back there with that four beats, you know.
Uh-huh. Let's talk about that. You said, 'The four beats, you know.' Everybody thinks that New Orleans music is two beat music, but that's not true.

Yeah. That's at the base of everything, that nice heartbeat. That's good, that four beats. So maybe in the revival music, the so-called Dixieland revival, maybe some of those people played more two beats. But Pops always played four, and he always said it was always -- you played four, and some of the books say that Walter Page, with Basie was one -- was the first person to play four beats. That's of course not true. So we're setting a lot of things straight, and that's good. Did -- in New Orleans, did they like the tuba in the bands or the string bass?
